classification.difficultyReason: Requires parameter-dependent double inequalities, recognition of an automatic lower bound, reversal when dividing by a negative parameter and symbolic number-line sketches.

content.prompt: Consider the inequality $a<|ax-b|<b$. For each of the following cases, solve the inequality in terms of $a$ and $b$, and sketch the solution on a number line.

answer.short:
$0<x<\frac ba-1$ or $\frac ba+1<x<\frac{2b}{a}$.

Split into the negative and positive branches of $ax-b$; all endpoints are excluded.
answer.worked:
The double inequality gives the two branches $-b<ax-b<-a$ or $a<ax-b<b$. Since $a>0$,
$$\begin{align*}-b&<ax-b<-a\\0&<ax<b-a\\0&<x<\frac ba-1.\end{align*}$$
For the positive branch,
$$\begin{align*}a&<ax-b<b\\a+b&<ax<2b\\\frac ba+1&<x<\frac{2b}{a}.\end{align*}$$
Thus $0<x<\frac ba-1$ or $\frac ba+1<x<\frac{2b}{a}$. Both intervals are non-empty because $\frac{b}{a}>1$. Use open endpoints.

spec.mathematics: 0 < b/a - 1 < b/a < b/a + 1 < 2b/a because b/a > 1. Symbolic schematic positions convey this ordering without assigning numerical parameter values.

answer.short:
$\frac{2b}{a}<x<0$.

The lower bound is automatic; dividing by $a<0$ reverses the inequalities.
answer.worked:
Since $a<0$ and $|ax-b|\ge0$, the condition $a<|ax-b|$ is always true. The remaining condition gives
$$\begin{align*}-b&<ax-b<b\\0&<ax<2b\\\frac{2b}{a}&<x<0.\end{align*}$$
The inequalities reverse when dividing by $a<0$. Both endpoints are excluded.
